chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Zurara, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God named a group of people who fasted when he broke the fast, and shortened [the prayer], as 'the disobedient ones', and said: 'They are the disobedient ones until the Day of Resurrection, and we indeed know their sons and the sons of their sons until our day today.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the 'disobedient ones' mentioned in the hadith regarding fasting during travel?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the specific ruling of fasting during travel by citing the Prophet’s designation of those who fasted while he did not as 'al-'Usaah' (the disobedient), a status that persists until the Day of Judgment. It further underscores the infallible Imams' unique ability to trace the lineage of these specific individuals, linking their historical action to their enduring spiritual identity in Shia tradition.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad, from Hareyz, from Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> named a group of people who were Fasting when he<sup>saww</sup> broke (the Fast), and shortened (the Prayer), as ‘disobedient ones’, and said: ‘They would be the disobedient ones up to the Day of Judgement, and we<sup>saww</sup> recognise their sons, and the sons of their sons up to this day of ours’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Hammad from Hariz from Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that

the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, named a people ‘disobedient’ when they fasted when he stopped fasting and reduced his Salat (prayer).’ He (the Imam) then said, ‘They are disobedient till this day and will remain so till the Day of Judgment. I know their children and the children of their children up to this, our day.’”
